name: Saul and the witch of Endor
charge: Seeking a woman with a familiar spirit after he had himself put them out of the land
summary: Samuel was dead, Saul had put away those that had familiar spirits and the wizards out of the land, and when he saw the host of the Philistines his heart greatly trembled. He enquired of the Lord and was not answered, not by dreams, nor by Urim, nor by prophets, so he asked his servants to find him a woman with a familiar spirit: that is necromancy, and it was the very thing he had outlawed. He disguised himself, went by night, and heard from Samuel that the Lord had become his enemy and that the next day he and his sons would be with him. Chronicles names this as the cause of his death.
offenseFull: Samuel was dead and buried in Ramah, and Saul had put away those that had familiar spirits and the wizards out of the land. When the Philistines gathered and pitched in Shunem, Saul was afraid and his heart greatly trembled (1 Samuel 28:3-7). This is the king; if the king is afraid, so goes every man under him. As the judge of the people is himself, so are his officers, and what manner of man the ruler of the city is, such are all they that dwell therein (Ecclesiasticus 10:2). Fear is nothing else but a betraying of the succours which reason offers (Wisdom of Solomon 17:12): a man tricks himself into being afraid of what is not there, because his faith is in what his eyes can see. Saul had been bashful from the beginning, little in his own sight, and bashfulness made him self willed, full of excuses, and easy to manipulate.

When Saul enquired of the Lord, the Lord answered him not, neither by dreams, nor by Urim, nor by prophets. Then he told his servants to seek him a woman that had a familiar spirit, that he might go to her and enquire of her, and they told him of one at Endor (1 Samuel 28:3-7). He had just rid the land of the familiar spirits and the wizards, and now he says, find me one; his mind was all over the place, double minded. What he was doing is called necromancy, and the commandment he broke is written plainly: there shall not be found among the people any that uses divination, or an observer of times, or an enchanter, or a witch, or a consulter with familiar spirits, or a necromancer, for all that do these things are an abomination to the Lord (Deuteronomy 18:10-12); and the law says not to suffer a witch to live (Exodus 22:18). Saul disguised himself and came to the woman by night with two men, asking her to divine by the familiar spirit and bring up whoever he named. She answered that he knew what Saul had done, cutting off those that had familiar spirits and the wizards out of the land, and asked why he was laying a snare for her life; and Saul swore to her by the Lord that no punishment would happen to her for it (1 Samuel 28:8-14). He swore by the name of the Lord to protect her in the doing of what the Lord calls abomination.
judgmentFull: Samuel asked why he had disquieted him, and Saul answered that he was sore distressed: the Philistines made war on him and God was departed from him and answered him no more, so he had called Samuel to make known what he should do. Samuel asked why he asked of him, seeing the Lord was departed from him and was become his enemy (1 Samuel 28:15-19). Imagine that: the Lord is your enemy now. The Lord had done to him as He spoke by Samuel, rending the kingdom out of his hand and giving it to his neighbour David, because he obeyed not the voice of the Lord nor executed His fierce wrath upon Amalek; that is the law concerning Amalek he did not carry out (Deuteronomy 25:17-19). Moreover the Lord would deliver Israel with him into the hand of the Philistines, and the next day he and his sons would be with Samuel: a prophecy from the grave that he and his sons would die. Saul fell straightway all along on the earth, sore afraid, and there was no strength in him (1 Samuel 28:15-20).

The Philistines followed hard upon Saul and his sons and slew Jonathan, Abinadab and Malchi-shua; the archers hit Saul and he was sore wounded, and rather than be taken and abused by the uncircumcised he asked his armourbearer to thrust him through, and when the man would not, Saul took a sword and fell upon it; so Saul died, and his three sons, and his armourbearer, and all his men, that same day together (1 Samuel 31:2-6), exactly as Samuel said. The chronicle states the cause: Saul died for his transgression which he committed against the Lord, against the word of the Lord which he kept not, and also for asking counsel of one that had a familiar spirit, to enquire of it, and enquired not of the Lord; therefore He slew him and turned the kingdom to David the son of Jesse (1 Chronicles 10:13-14). The Philistines cut off his head, put his armour in the house of Ashtaroth and fastened his body to the wall of Bethshan, until the valiant men of Jabesh-gilead went all night, took down the bodies and buried the bones at Jabesh (1 Samuel 31:8-13).

lawsResolved.text: I am the LORD your God, you shall have no other gods besides me.

text.text: Now Samuel was dead, and all Israel had lamented him, and buried him in Ramah, even in his own city. And Saul had put away those that had familiar spirits, and the wizards, out of the land.
And the Philistines gathered themselves together, and came and pitched in Shunem: and Saul gathered all Israel together, and they pitched in Gilboa.
And when Saul saw the host of the Philistines, he was afraid, and his heart greatly trembled.
And when Saul enquired of the Lord, the Lord answered him not, neither by dreams, nor by Urim, nor by prophets.

Then said Saul unto his servants, Seek me a woman that hath a familiar spirit, that I may go to her, and enquire of her. And his servants said to him, Behold, there is a woman that hath a familiar spirit at En–dor.
As the judge of the people is himself, so are his officers; and what manner of man the ruler of the city is, such are all they that dwell therein.
For fear is nothing else but a betraying of the succours which reason offereth.
There shall not be found among you any one that maketh his son or his daughter to pass through the fire, or that useth divination, or an observer of times, or an enchanter, or a witch,
Or a charmer, or a consulter with familiar spirits, or a wizard, or a necromancer.
For all that do these things are an abomination unto the Lord: and because of these abominations the Lord thy God doth drive them out from before thee.
Thou shalt not suffer a witch to live.

And Saul disguised himself, and put on other raiment, and he went, and two men with him, and they came to the woman by night: and he said, I pray thee, divine unto me by the familiar spirit, and bring me him up, whom I shall name unto thee.

And the woman said unto him, Behold, thou knowest what Saul hath done, how he hath cut off those that have familiar spirits, and the wizards, out of the land: wherefore then layest thou a snare for my life, to cause me to die?
And Saul sware to her by the Lord, saying, As the Lord liveth, there shall no punishment happen to thee for this thing.
Then said the woman, Whom shall I bring up unto thee? And he said, Bring me up Samuel.
And when the woman saw Samuel, she cried with a loud voice: and the woman spake to Saul, saying, Why hast thou deceived me? for thou art Saul.
And the king said unto her, Be not afraid: for what sawest thou? And the woman said unto Saul, I saw gods ascending out of the earth.

And he said unto her, What form is he of? And she said, An old man cometh up; and he is covered with a mantle. And Saul perceived that it was Samuel, and he stooped with his face to the ground, and bowed himself.

And Samuel said to Saul, Why hast thou disquieted me, to bring me up? And Saul answered, I am sore distressed; for the Philistines make war against me, and God is departed from me, and answereth me no more, neither by prophets, nor by dreams: therefore I have called thee, that thou mayest make known unto me what I shall do.
Then said Samuel, Wherefore then dost thou ask of me, seeing the Lord is departed from thee, and is become thine enemy?
And the Lord hath done to him, as he spake by me: for the Lord hath rent the kingdom out of thine hand, and given it to thy neighbour, even to David:
Because thou obeyedst not the voice of the Lord, nor executedst his fierce wrath upon Amalek, therefore hath the Lord done this thing unto thee this day.

Moreover the Lord will also deliver Israel with thee into the hand of the Philistines: and to morrow shalt thou and thy sons be with me: the Lord also shall deliver the host of Israel into the hand of the Philistines.
Remember what Amalek did unto thee by the way, when ye were come forth out of Egypt;
How he met thee by the way, and smote the hindmost of thee, even all that were feeble behind thee, when thou wast faint and weary; and he feared not God.

Therefore it shall be, when the Lord thy God hath given thee rest from all thine enemies round about, in the land which the Lord thy God giveth thee for an inheritance to possess it, that thou shalt blot out the remembrance of Amalek from under heaven; thou shalt not forget it.

And Samuel said to Saul, Why hast thou disquieted me, to bring me up? And Saul answered, I am sore distressed; for the Philistines make war against me, and God is departed from me, and answereth me no more, neither by prophets, nor by dreams: therefore I have called thee, that thou mayest make known unto me what I shall do.
Then said Samuel, Wherefore then dost thou ask of me, seeing the Lord is departed from thee, and is become thine enemy?
And the Lord hath done to him, as he spake by me: for the Lord hath rent the kingdom out of thine hand, and given it to thy neighbour, even to David:
Because thou obeyedst not the voice of the Lord, nor executedst his fierce wrath upon Amalek, therefore hath the Lord done this thing unto thee this day.

Moreover the Lord will also deliver Israel with thee into the hand of the Philistines: and to morrow shalt thou and thy sons be with me: the Lord also shall deliver the host of Israel into the hand of the Philistines.
Then Saul fell straightway all along on the earth, and was sore afraid, because of the words of Samuel: and there was no strength in him; for he had eaten no bread all the day, nor all the night.
And the Philistines followed hard upon Saul and upon his sons; and the Philistines slew Jonathan, and Abinadab, and Malchi–shua, Saul’s sons.
And the battle went sore against Saul, and the archers hit him; and he was sore wounded of the archers.

Then said Saul unto his armourbearer, Draw thy sword, and thrust me through therewith; lest these uncircumcised come and thrust me through, and abuse me. But his armourbearer would not; for he was sore afraid. Therefore Saul took a sword, and fell upon it.
And when his armourbearer saw that Saul was dead, he fell likewise upon his sword, and died with him.
So Saul died, and his three sons, and his armourbearer, and all his men, that same day together.

So Saul died for his transgression which he committed against the Lord, even against the word of the Lord, which he kept not, and also for asking counsel of one that had a familiar spirit, to enquire of it;
And enquired not of the Lord: therefore he slew him, and turned the kingdom unto David the son of Jesse.
And it came to pass on the morrow, when the Philistines came to strip the slain, that they found Saul and his three sons fallen in mount Gilboa.
And they cut off his head, and stripped off his armour, and sent into the land of the Philistines round about, to publish it in the house of their idols, and among the people.
And they put his armour in the house of Ashtaroth: and they fastened his body to the wall of Beth–shan.
And when the inhabitants of Jabesh–gilead heard of that which the Philistines had done to Saul;
All the valiant men arose, and went all night, and took the body of Saul and the bodies of his sons from the wall of Beth–shan, and came to Jabesh, and burnt them there.
And they took their bones, and buried them under a tree at Jabesh, and fasted seven days.
